explanation: The Wilton article makes the 1690 raid the reason the 1693 one could be found at all: "In sixteen days they reached the Mohawk, led by a guide captured in the Schenectady Massacre, Jan Baptiste Van Eps." The same man then undid it — "Van Eps had escaped before the attacks and made his way to Schenectady, where he alerted the inhabitants to the French attack" — which is how Schuyler came to be on the retreat road. Enabled and not caused: Schenectady did not decide that the Mohawk castles would be attacked, it supplied the man who led the way there. Wikipedia is the only author named, so probable.
